newsitem.title: USA: US jet fuel tracks NYMEX gains, Gulf diffs decline.
newsitem.headline: US jet fuel tracks NYMEX gains, Gulf diffs decline.

text.p: jumped higher Tuesday, tracking strong gains in NYMEX futures on expectations of stock draws in today's weekly API inventory reports, traders said.

However, Gulf Coast differentials eased as buyers resisted the NYMEX movement, market players said. Aviation-quality 54-grade for prompt shipment on the Colonial Pipeline was traded at 1.40 cents under the print, while late November material was put between 1.25 and 1.50 cents under the print.
"As the screen rallies, people aren't willing to pay up," according to one trader.
The USG low sulphur "55" grade market remained lethargic, with prompt barrels put between 0.25 cents on either side of the NYMEX.
New York Harbor 54-grade prices also moved higher on the back of the NYMEX, though diffs slipped to between 2.00 to 2.25 cents, down about 0.25 cents from Monday.
